intro: The standing rules are the constraints the owner has ratified that hold for every block of work and every design, now and later. They are not promises or quality targets: they say what the engine must do or must never do, whatever shape the design takes. The panel and the design rounds must respect every one of them, and a design that breaks one is out.

They come from the roadmap's section on standing constraints, in its six groups: identity and player data; growth without corners; the media model; the design-iteration loop; platform parity; and the engine holds no opinion. The identity rules are also the privacy defaults that every future operator of the open-source engine inherits. Each rule below says where it comes from and, where the roadmap gives one, the date the owner ratified it.

rules.title: Players never have accounts
rules.line: Players never have accounts. Nothing a player uses, a phone or a scanner, ever asks a player to log in.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, identity and player data, rule 1; ratified 2026-08-29, reaffirming the engine's one design for who gets access.

rules.title: The engine knows devices, not people
rules.line: The only identity built into the engine is a device id or a session id. Naming a person is game policy, never an engine default.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, identity and player data, rule 2.

rules.title: How players are identified is the game's choice
rules.line: A game may add its own ways to identify players with whatever its hardware allows: a typed name on a personal phone, a scanned object such as a band or a character token at a shared station, or nothing at all. Letting a player claim credit is one optional pattern for games on personal devices, not a platform rule.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, identity and player data, rule 2.

rules.title: Game data stays on the kit
rules.line: Game data stays on the kit unless the owner moves it.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, identity and player data, rule 3.

rules.title: The owner sets how long data is kept
rules.line: How long old game data is kept is the owner's decision, made per game.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, identity and player data, rule 4.

rules.title: Never assume one kit, one pack, one production
rules.line: No block may build in the assumption of one kit, one pack or one production where avoiding it costs little. The seams that make more possible are built now; the features that use them belong to the operations era.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, growth without corners; ratified 2026-08-29.

rules.title: Pack and venue profile chosen, never assumed
rules.line: The pack is chosen by path or id and never assumed to be the only one. The venue profile is chosen the same way.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, growth without corners, the design-document checklist.

rules.title: No one kit's names inside engine code
rules.line: Engine code never contains an identifier that belongs to one kit.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, growth without corners, the design-document checklist.

rules.title: Network names and addresses work per kit
rules.line: The way the kit's devices find each other by name and address works for each kit on its own.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, growth without corners, the design-document checklist.

rules.title: Media never lives inside the pack
rules.line: Media files never live inside the pack, and carrying them there is out of this era entirely. The pack names its media files, each with a fingerprint of its contents.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, the media model; ratified 2026-08-29, with the out-of-era ruling of the same date.

rules.title: A managed media bundle carries the files
rules.line: A managed media bundle, kept apart from the pack, carries the actual files. The hardware scanner already gets its files this way, and that is the model.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, the media model; ratified 2026-08-29.

rules.title: A designer can upload the pack's media
rules.line: A designer can work through the files their pack needs and upload them through the design tool.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, the media model, requirement (a) on the final tool.

rules.title: Media bundles move between machines
rules.line: A bundle can be checked against the pack's list of files and moved easily between engine machines for different game instances.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, the media model, requirement (b) on the final tool.

rules.title: Games are playtested without code or settings files
rules.line: A designer makes a game playtestable without writing code or editing a settings file: change a value in the tool, apply it, playtest, repeat. Making this possible is the point of the engine work.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, the design-iteration loop; ratified 2026-08-29.

rules.title: The editor and live apply ship together
rules.line: The mechanics editor is where the loop happens, and applying a change while the engine runs, between games, is what makes the loop fast instead of a restart per change. The editor and that apply ship together as one deliverable.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, the design-iteration loop, the ratified floor.

rules.title: Phones and hardware scanners stay equal in ability
rules.line: Phones and other web devices stay equal to the hardware scanners in what the engine lets them do. Both can drive the same interactions the pack declares, including multi-tap player actions.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, platform parity; ratified 2026-08-29, reaffirming the ruling of 2026-07-18 that the hardware scanner is a first-class platform.

rules.title: Equal in ability, not in screens
rules.line: Parity does not mean identical screens: a keyboard, a screen size and a personal or shared device differ. A game's kit declares which kinds of device its players use and what part each plays.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, platform parity; ratified 2026-08-29.

rules.title: Hardware scanner work waits on no game
rules.line: Bringing the hardware scanner's code up to parity is platform work the engine commits to. It does not wait on any one game's design.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, platform parity; ratified 2026-08-29.

rules.title: Designers change pack data, never device code
rules.line: Everything a designer iterates on is pack data, never the code built into a device. Never design a mechanic that can only be tuned by reloading the code on every hardware scanner.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, platform parity, the standing principle; ratified 2026-08-29.

rules.title: The engine holds no opinion on game design
rules.line: Game-design choices are pack and kit parameters, never engine defaults: how players are identified, rosters, how scarce stations are, what is tracked, and whether more engagement is better.
rules.source: Roadmap, standing constraints, the engine holds no opinion; reaffirmed 2026-08-29.
